opening.quote: Agent: morning, Tidewell homes, my name is brum. How can't I hell you?
opening.comment: The agent gives a company name and their own name, though the name is garbled as 'brum' and the greeting is muddled, so the opening is only partly clear; the criterion is met on substance.

verification.quote: Agent: Can I have your full name and number or
verification.comment: The agent asked for name and order number before discussing the order, but the customer gave name and order number, and the agent then discussed the order; verification was requested before sharing data, so this passes.

understanding.quote: Agent: So the bookcase arrived but the bag of screw was missing?
understanding.comment: The agent captured the issue (missing screws) and confirmed it, though it asked about the bookcase arrival after the caller already described it.

resolution_accuracy.quote: Agent: You'll need to return the wholes bookcase and order it again.
resolution_accuracy.comment: Missing parts are sent free within 3 working days with no return needed, so telling the customer to return the bookcase and reorder is incorrect per policy.

process_compliance.comment: The agent did not offer to send the missing part free within 3 working days and did not ask permission before any hold, so required handling was not followed.

communication.comment: The caller said they were frustrated and the agent dismissed the issue without acknowledging the frustration, and the tone was rude.

closing.comment: The call ended without confirming what happens next or asking if there is anything else, and without a polite close.
